purpose: Fixture round for working on the UI without an agent attached. Exercises every card state: open with options, awaiting an agent reply, clarified but still open, settled, and rejected.

questions.title: Where does session state live?
questions.body:
Scratch state is meaningless once the session ends, but the docs phase reads from it. That pulls in two directions.

questions.title: Should the agent long-poll or should we push?
questions.body: Both consumers need to know when state moved. One primitive can serve them if the browser waits on a version and the agent waits on a predicate.

entries.body: Does SSE not give us reconnect for free?
It does, but the agent still needs a blocking call it can background, and that is not SSE-shaped. One primitive covers both consumers; SSE would sit alongside it rather than replace it.

questions.title: Who assigns question IDs?
questions.body: If the agent picks them, a typo silently splits a thread in two.
options: The agent, in the round payload

entries.body: Recorded. ask returns the assigned IDs so the agent learns them rather than inventing them.

questions.title: Ship a bundled Mermaid runtime for diagrams?
questions.body: Roughly 1MB of vendored JavaScript, in exchange for diagram syntax the agent already knows.

entries.body: Recorded as rejected. Diagrams stay as agent-authored inline SVG and the page keeps zero dependencies.

questions.title: What closes a grilling session?
questions.body: The cleanup and docs pickers do not need their own UI — they are just a final round of ordinary questions.
